titleStmt.title: Memorandum From Roger Fontaine of the National Security Council Staff to the President’s Assistant for National Security Affairs (Allen)

div.head: 462. Memorandum From Roger Fontaine of the National Security Council Staff to the President’s Assistant for National Security Affairs (Allen)

list.label: SUBJECT
list.item: The President’s Letter to Venezuelan President Herrera Campins (U)

div.p: At Tab B is Secretary Haig’s memorandum summarizing President Herrera’s letter to the President and the current status of relations with Venezuela. Secretary Haig notes our commonly held views vis-a-vis Cuba and the Duarte government in El Salvador. The Secretary also recommends that we hold up notification re the sale of F–16s to Venezuela until the exchange of the Presidents is complete. (C)

At Tab A is the President’s response to President Herrera, which covers the pertinent issues including a gentle critique of President Herrera’s proposal that Latin America be a “zone of peace,” a concept that implies the US should have no responsibilities in the region. At Tab I is your memorandum to the President recommending that he sign the letter to President Herrera Campins. (C)
NOTE: Foreign Minister Zambrano of Venezuela indicated a strong interest in a September meeting of the two Presidents. This was not an “official request” but it was proposed to Ambassador Luers. (C)
That you sign the memorandum at Tab I. (U)
The President’s reply at Tab A has been cleared with the speechwriters. (U)

note.p: Source: Reagan Library, Roger W. Fontaine Files, Subject File, Venezuela [04/01/1981–04/15/1981]. Confidential. Sent for action. Copies were sent to Timothy Deal and Carole Farrar of the National Security Council staff.

Tab A was not found. A signed copy of Reagan’s April 21 letter to Herrera and an initialed copy of Allen’s April 17 covering memorandum to Reagan are in the Reagan Library, Roger W. W. Fontaine Files, Subject File, Venezuela [04/16/1981–04/30/1981].
Attached but not printed, is an undated and uninitialed memorandum from Allen to Reagan.
